build.prompt_version: Trump Diary — Weekly Thread Package Prompt v1

week.headline: The thirteenth week of Trump’s second term did not hinge on a single order or speech.
week.summary: The thirteenth week of Trump’s second term did not hinge on a single order or speech. Its shape emerged from the way power was used across many fronts at once: in courts and prisons, on campuses and trading floors, inside agencies and newsrooms. What tied these moves together was not noise but method. Law, money, and information were bent toward the same end—making loyalty safer than dissent, and turning the costs of resistance into a quiet, daily fact of life.

evidence_items.why_it_matters: The week’s own framing emphasizes governing by method across institutions rather than a single policy event, matching the constitutional pattern of broad executive aggrandizement.

evidence_items.title: Law, money, and information bent toward one end
evidence_items.why_it_matters: This identifies a presidency using multiple governing levers at once while weakening ordinary checks and making resistance costly.

evidence_items.title: Court-centered and agency-centered confrontations recur through the week
evidence_items.why_it_matters: Court conflict and unilateral pressure across domains are core markers of this thread.

thread_states.summary: This week is strongly legible as another chapter in executive maximalism: not a single spectacular emergency act, but a continuing pattern of presidential power expanding through dispersed pressure on courts, agencies, and other institutions.
continuity_notes: Carries forward the prior weeks’ pattern of weakening checks through accumulation rather than one dramatic rupture.
Should be written as the constitutional method underneath several other week-level developments, not as an isolated legal subplot.

continuity_notes: Build on prior-week legal retaliation and selective-enforcement patterns rather than introducing this as new.

week_summary_notes: This week is best understood as a multi-front demonstration of governing method rather than a single dominant event.
The strongest collision is among executive overreach, weaponized law, and information control; together they explain why the week feels systematic rather than episodic.
Administrative capture and crony political economy matter as enabling machinery and incentive structure, but they should not displace the legal-information frame.
Campus pressure is important because it localizes the week’s broader method inside semi-independent institutions that can host dissent.

Immigration and stratified-rights themes remain part of the larger backdrop, but this week’s emphasis is less about status categories themselves than about the coordinated use of institutions to enforce compliance.
The week should close on normalization: coercion appearing as ordinary administration across many venues at once.

rewrite_guidance.opening_focus: Open by stressing that the week’s significance lay in coordinated method across institutions—courts, agencies, campuses, markets, and media—rather than in a single proclamation. Frame executive power, legal asymmetry, and information control as the three main operating logics.
rewrite_guidance.closing_focus: Close on the normalization of coercive governance: loyalty made safer than dissent, resistance converted into a daily cost, and state, market, and information systems increasingly aligned in the same direction.
continuity_emphasis_notes: Emphasize continuity from prior weeks by showing that the administration no longer needs one spectacular rupture; dispersed pressure now performs the same work.
Link legal, informational, and administrative developments as mutually reinforcing rather than as separate issue silos.
Treat campus and market developments as proof that the week’s method extended beyond Washington institutions into civil society and economic life.
Keep any mention of immigration or rights hierarchy brief unless a concrete event in the source text demands expansion.
Do not overstate resistance; the week’s narrative energy comes from the accumulation of pressure, not from successful pushback.
